title: Structured Machine Theory of Mind from Agent Trajectories
abstract: arXiv:2611.07208v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Predictive models of human behavior trained on large-scale trajectory data optimize for statistical accuracy without representing the mental states that causally generate behavior. Such models support prediction but not principled intervention: they cannot answer how an agent's behavior would change if its beliefs or preferences were different. We introduce Structured Machine Theory of Mind (SMToM), a framework that attributes explicit, independently supervised belief and desire representations from observed trajectories within a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) causal structure. The central architectural element is a goal head that consumes only the predicted mental-state channels and a current-trajectory embedding; counterfactual intervention on beliefs and desires is a direct operation. translated_title: 从智能体轨迹构建结构化机器心智理论
translated_abstract: 在大规模轨迹数据上训练的人类行为预测模型，其优化目标是统计准确性，却未能表征那些因果性生成行为的心理状态。这类模型支持预测，但不支持有原则的干预：它们无法回答“如果智能体的信念或偏好不同，其行为会如何变化”这类问题。我们提出结构化机器心智理论，这是一个在信念-愿望-意图（BDI）因果结构内，从观测到的轨迹中归因出显式的、可独立监督的信念与愿望表征的框架。其核心架构元素是一个目标头，该目标头仅消费预测出的心理状态通道以及当前轨迹嵌入；由此，对信念和愿望的反事实干预成为直接操作。我们在一个受控行人导航领域中实例化了SMToM，该领域中真实心理状态是通过构造方式已知的，从而能够对归因质量进行评估。
tldr: 本文提出SMToM框架，在信念-愿望-意图（BDI）因果结构下从智能体轨迹中归因出显式且独立监督的信念与愿望表征，使得对智能体心理状态的反事实干预成为直接操作，超越了仅做统计预测的行为模型。
en_tdlr: SMToM attributes explicit, independently supervised belief and desire representations from agent trajectories within a BDI causal structure, enabling direct counterfactual intervention on an agent's mental states beyond mere statistical behavior prediction.
